skill.name: risk-metrics-calculation

content.value_statement: Portfolio risk decisions need consistent VaR, drawdown, and risk-adjusted return measures. This skill provides reusable patterns for calculating and reviewing those metrics.
actual_capabilities: Calculates volatility, downside deviation, beta, historical VaR, parametric VaR, Cornish-Fisher VaR, and CVaR.
Computes maximum drawdown, average drawdown, drawdown duration, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, Calmar ratio, and Omega ratio.
Analyzes portfolio volatility, marginal risk contribution, component risk, correlation, diversification ratio, and tracking error.
Provides rolling volatility, rolling Sharpe, rolling VaR, rolling drawdown, rolling beta, and volatility regime patterns.
Includes historical, hypothetical, and Monte Carlo stress testing examples for portfolio return series.
limitations: The skill provides implementation patterns, not validated production risk infrastructure.
Users must supply clean return series, benchmark data, asset weights, and historical scenario data.
Examples assume common daily trading conventions and may need adjustment for other markets.
The skill does not provide investment advice or regulatory certification.

use_cases.title: Portfolio Risk Review
use_cases.description: Measure portfolio losses, drawdowns, and risk-adjusted returns before a rebalance.

use_cases.title: Risk Analytics Prototype
use_cases.description: Build Python classes for VaR, CVaR, rolling risk, and portfolio contribution analysis.

use_cases.title: Risk Report Preparation
use_cases.description: Create consistent metrics for daily or monthly risk monitoring reports.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Portfolio Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to calculate historical VaR, CVaR, maximum drawdown, Sharpe ratio, and Sortino ratio for my daily returns. Explain assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare VaR Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare historical, parametric, and Cornish-Fisher VaR for my return series. Explain when each method can mislead.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Portfolio Contributions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to calculate portfolio volatility, component risk, marginal risk contribution, diversification ratio, and tracking error from my asset returns and weights.

prompt_templates.title: Design Stress Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design rolling risk metrics, volatility regimes, historical stress tests, hypothetical shocks, and Monte Carlo stress checks for a dashboard.

output_examples.input: Daily returns for an equity portfolio and a two percent risk-free rate.
output_examples.output: A concise risk summary with annual volatility, historical VaR, CVaR, maximum drawdown, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, skewness, and kurtosis.

output_examples.input: Asset return columns, portfolio weights, and benchmark returns.
output_examples.output: A portfolio risk review showing volatility, risk contribution by asset, diversification ratio, correlation matrix, and tracking error.

output_examples.input: Portfolio returns, historical crisis data, and hypothetical asset shocks.
output_examples.output: A stress test summary with scenario loss, maximum drawdown, worst day, elevated-volatility VaR, and probability of a ten percent loss.

best_practices: Use several risk metrics because one measure cannot describe all portfolio risk.
Check rolling metrics because risk levels change across market regimes.
Document assumptions for confidence levels, lookback windows, annualization, and return cleaning.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on VaR alone when tail losses are important.
Do not assume returns are normal without checking skewness and kurtosis.
Do not use short lookback windows without testing regime sensitivity.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs return series, and some workflows also need asset weights, benchmark returns, or historical scenario data.

faq.question: Can it calculate both VaR and CVaR?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes historical VaR, parametric VaR, Cornish-Fisher VaR, and conditional VaR examples.

faq.question: Does it support portfolio-level analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers portfolio volatility, risk contribution, diversification ratio, correlations, and tracking error.

faq.question: Can it monitor changing risk over time?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes rolling volatility, rolling Sharpe, rolling VaR, rolling drawdown, beta, and regime classification.

faq.question: Does it provide financial advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides calculation patterns and risk analysis structure, not investment recommendations.
